lines.text: Which hand aged? After four and a half years, one group showed no extra ageing.
lines.phonemes: wˌɪtʃ hˈand ˈeɪdʒd? ˈaftə fˈɔː and ɐ hˈɑːf jˈiəz, wˈɒn ɡɹˈuːp ʃˈəʊd nˈəʊ ˈɛkstɹəɹ ˈeɪdʒɪŋ.

lines.text: In Nambour, Australia, pure chance decided who would wear sunscreen every morning. Head, neck, arms and hands, before the day began.
lines.phonemes: ˈɪn nˈæmbɔː , ɒstɹˈeɪliə, pjˈʊə tʃˈans dɪsˈaɪdɪd hˌuː wʊd wˈeə sˈʌnskɹiːn ˈɛvɹɪ mˈɔːnɪŋ. hˈɛd, nˈɛk, ˈɑːmz and hˈandz, bɪfˌɔː ðə dˈeɪ bɪɡˈan.

lines.text: The other group could use sunscreen whenever they liked. Researchers then measured the fine lines on silicone copies of hands.
lines.phonemes: ðɪ ˈʌðə ɡɹˈuːp kʊd jˈuːz sˈʌnskɹiːn wɛnˌɛvə ðeɪ lˈaɪkt. ɹɪsˈɜːtʃəz ðˈɛn mˈɛʒəd ðə fˈaɪn lˈaɪnz ˌɒn sˈɪlɪkˌəʊn kˈɒpɪz ɒv hˈandz.

lines.text: It is easy to think sun damage is the burn you feel. But an ultraviolet camera shows damage your eyes miss, long before it appears on the surface.
lines.phonemes: ɪt ɪz ˈiːzi tə θˈɪŋk sˈʌn dˈamɪdʒ ɪz ðə bˈɜːn juː fˈiːl. bˌʌt ɐn ˌʊltɹɐvˈaɪəlɪt kˈamɹə ʃˈəʊz dˈamɪdʒ jɔːɹ ˈaɪz mˈɪs, lˈɒŋ bɪfˌɔːɹ ɪt ɐpˈiəz ɒnðə sˈɜːfɪs.

lines.text: Ten years later, they checked again. Melanoma, the most serious skin cancer, was about half as common in that group, though the numbers were small.
lines.phonemes: tˈɛn jˈiəz lˈeɪtə, ðeɪ tʃˈɛkt ɐɡˈɛn. mˌɛlənˈəʊmə , ðə mˈəʊst sˈiəɹiəs skˈɪn kˈansə, wɒz ɐbˌaʊt hˈɑːf az kˈɒmən ɪn ðat ɡɹˈuːp, ðˌəʊ ðə nˈʌmbəz wɜː smˈɔːl.

lines.text: At a lab's test dose, a layer of sunscreen is about a fifth as thick as a sheet of paper.
lines.phonemes: atə lˈabz tˈɛst dˈəʊs, ɐ lˈeɪəɹ ɒv sˈʌnskɹiːn ɪz ɐbˌaʊt ɐ fˈɪfθ az θˈɪk az ɐ ʃˈiːt ɒv pˈeɪpə.

lines.text: So, which hand aged? Both groups missed some mornings. One missed fewer, and the skin kept count.
lines.phonemes: sˈəʊ, wˌɪtʃ hˈand ˈeɪdʒd? bˈəʊθ ɡɹˈuːps mˈɪst sˌʌm mˈɔːnɪŋz. wˈɒn mˈɪst fjˈuːə, and ðə skˈɪn kˈɛpt kˈaʊnt.

lines.text: Next: tanning beds share a list with cigarettes. Same list, same risk?
